For anyone waiting on this: @TheOutdoorProgrammer's PR #12520 had accumulated merge conflicts with current `dev`. I've rebased it onto current `upstream/dev`, resolved all conflicts, and fixed a few bugs found during testing (broken tool parameter schema, LLM parameter name hallucination). See [my comment on PR #12520](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/12520#issuecomment-4404159450) for details.

**If you want to use it today**, you can build from my fork:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/stephanschielke/opencode
cd opencode
git checkout fix/mcp-lazy-rebased-for-upstream
cd packages/opencode && bun install && bun run build
```

Then add to your `opencode.json`:

```json
{
  "experimental": {
    "mcp_lazy": true
  }
}
```

This replaces all MCP tool schemas in context with a single `mcp_search` tool (~620 tokens). Agents call `mcp_search(operation: "list"|"search"|"describe"|"call", ...)` to discover and invoke MCP tools on demand. Tested with 9 connected MCP servers — saves ~21k tokens per prompt (for me)!

Also wanted to echo @laradji's point from the PR — local models finally work much better given the smaller initial context required. This is a real quality-of-life improvement for anyone running local/smaller models.

Thanks to @TheOutdoorProgrammer for the original implementation — really glad we found exactly what we were looking for instead of having to start from scratch!

Hey @TheOutdoorProgrammer — I've been using this and it's great work! Your branch has merge conflicts with current `dev` though, so I rebased it and fixed a few bugs along the way.

**Ready-to-use branch:** [`stephanschielke/opencode:fix/mcp-lazy-rebased-for-upstream`](https://github.com/stephanschielke/opencode/tree/fix/mcp-lazy-rebased-for-upstream)

This is your original commit cherry-picked onto current `upstream/dev` HEAD with conflicts resolved + fixes. You can pull it and force-push to update this PR:

```bash
git remote add stephanschielke https://github.com/stephanschielke/opencode.git
git fetch stephanschielke fix/mcp-lazy-rebased-for-upstream
git checkout dev
git reset --hard stephanschielke/fix/mcp-lazy-rebased-for-upstream
git push --force-with-lease origin dev
```

**Fixes included on top of your original commit:**

- **`Schema.Struct` for parameters** — the original used `Schema.Unknown` which rendered as `{}` to the LLM. Models had no JSON schema to anchor on and hallucinated wrong param names. Now uses a proper typed struct.
- **Parameter alias normalization** — weaker models (e.g. minimax) consistently send `mcp_name`/`tool_name`/`arguments` instead of `server`/`tool`/`args`. Added transparent fallback aliases.
- **Updated `mcp-search.txt`** — explicit parameter names, workflow examples, and "do NOT use" warning for hallucinated names.
- **`Effect.serviceOption`** — MCP dependency is optional in ToolRegistry so the tool only initializes when `mcp_lazy: true`, preventing crashes when MCP.Service isn't provided.
- **Test compatibility** — updated `system.test.ts` and `registry.test.ts` with MCP/Config mock layers.
- **Full architecture port** — `mcp-search.ts` rewritten from async namespace to current Effect service pattern; `system.ts` `mcpServers()` ported to Effect method.

All tested end-to-end against 9 connected MCP servers. Happy to adjust anything!

Diagnosis — this is in `@opentui/solid`, not opencode itself.

`packages/solid/src/reconciler.ts` calls `decodeHTML` from the `entities` package on every text-node create/replace and on `text` / `content` prop sets. Added in https://github.com/sst/opentui/pull/780 to keep `<` and `>` in JSX text from rendering as `<` / `>`. But `decodeHTML` is the full HTML5 named-entity decoder, so it also resolves `&para`, `&times`, `&amp`, etc:

```js
import { decodeHTML } from "entities"
decodeHTML("&parameter") // → "¶meter"
decodeHTML("&times")     // → "×"
```

I checked whether this leaks past display by logging the bytes inside `submit()` in `packages/opencode/src/cli/cmd/tui/component/prompt/index.tsx` — both `store.prompt.input` and the textarea's `plainText` carry `&parameter` raw at submit time. So the wire is intact; the LLM receives exactly what was typed. The reason the WebFetch URL *looks* decoded in the status output is that the rendered chat bubble (which echoes both the user message and the tool response body) goes through the same opentui-solid reconciler, so anything matching an HTML entity reference gets visually decoded.

The fix needs to land upstream — swap the broad `decodeHTML(value)` for a narrow unescape covering only the five entities Solid actually emits (`<`, `>`, `&`, `"`, `'`).

> When configuring Google Stitch as a remote MCP server in opencode, the error "stitch Failed to get tools" appears and Stitch tools are not loaded.
> 
> ### Environment
> * opencode version: 1.14.33
> * OS: macOS

>

> {
>   "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json",
>   "mcp": {
>     "stitch": {
>       "type": "remote",
>       "url": "https://stitch.googleapis.com/mcp",
>       "enabled": true,
>       "headers": {
>         "X-Goog-Api-Key": "<API_KEY>"
>       }
>     }
>   }
> }
> ### What works
> * Direct curl to Stitch endpoint with POST returns tools correctly
> * The Stitch API responds correctly (405 on GET, 200 on POST with tools)
> 
> ### What doesn't work
> * opencode fails to load Stitch MCP tools despite API key being valid, config correct, and API responding properly to direct requests

> 1. Config with only Stitch MCP (no other providers/MCP servers) → Same error

> ### Conclusion
> Bug in how opencode 1.14.33 handles the `X-Goog-Api-Key` header for remote MCP servers, or how it parses the response from Google's Stitch MCP endpoint.
>

> * [Agents and Commands are not shown #8868](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/issues/8868) - Similar MCP remote server issues
>

> Stitch MCP tools should be available in opencode when configured correctly.

## Technical findings from same environment

Confirmed the same freeze behavior on Windows with v1.14.41. Investigation of the diff v1.14.40..v1.14.41 found:

### Bug found and patched
packages/desktop/src/main/apps.ts: resolveWindowsAppPath calls execFilePromise(where, [appName]).toString() without await, always returning [object Promise] instead of the resolved path on Windows.

PR: https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/26319

### Other observations from logs (Windows Desktop v1.14.41)

The sidecar process starts and then exits with code 0 after approximately 5 seconds. The main log shows: server ready at T+2s, then sidecar exited { code: 0 } at T+5s. App restarts and loops.

This may be related to the utilityProcess.fork sidecar refactor in v1.14.41 (commit 54a78c922). HEAD already has a major refactor to Effect-TS for the main process, likely targeting stability.

- Windows 11
- OpenCode Desktop v1.14.41 (auto-updated from v1.14.39)
- Providers: openai, minimax-coding-plan, opencode-go, github-copilot
- No npx-based MCP servers configured (rules out #26012)

## Deep Analysis: Local Session Data (Last 100 Sessions)

Analyzed \`opencode.db\` for the last 100 sessions. Found **31 compaction events** across these sessions, with **3 errors** total (2 UnknownError jinja template failures, 1 MessageAbortedError).

### Key Finding: Empty User Messages After Compaction

Examined the \`witty-island\` session (the one with the jinja error) and found a clear pattern:

**Message sequence:**
1. **msg#8**: Successful compaction (in=1612, out=297 tokens) - triggered by auto-compaction
2. **msg#9**: Synthetic user message with \`metadata.compaction_continue=True\`, text: "Continue if you have next steps, or stop and ask for clarification..."
3. **msg#10**: Synthetic user message with \`type='compaction'\`, \`auto=True\`, \`tail_start_id=msg#9\`
4. **msg#11**: Failed compaction (in=0, out=0) - jinja error: "No user query found in messages"

The \`part\` table stores message content separately from the \`message\` table. Messages 9 and 10 have no content in their message data - only synthetic metadata parts.

### Root Cause Hypothesis

The sequence is:
1. Auto-compaction triggers after context grows large (msg#7 → msg#8)
2. Compaction succeeds, creating a summary
3. opencode creates a synthetic "continue" user message (msg#9) to resume the conversation
4. Auto-compaction triggers AGAIN because context is still large (msg#10)
5. Second compaction fails because LM Studio's Qwen3 jinja template can't find a valid user query

The issue is that when opencode builds the prompt for the second compaction, it includes msg#9 (synthetic "continue" message) and msg#10 (auto-compaction trigger). LM Studio's Qwen3 jinja template strictly requires at least one user message with text content. The synthetic messages either:
- Are filtered out before reaching the model (leaving no user messages)
- Are not recognized as valid "user queries" by the jinja template

### Provider-Specific Issue

This error is **specific to LM Studio's Qwen3 model** (\`root-lmstudio\`). The other 28 successful auto-compactions in the same 100-session window used Anthropic (Claude) and did not fail. The jinja template error message itself is from LM Studio, confirming this is a provider-specific prompt rendering issue.

### Recommended Fixes

**Short-term (opencode side):**
- When building compaction prompts, ensure at least one valid user message with text content is always included
- Filter out synthetic messages (\`synthetic=True\`) before sending to providers with strict jinja templates
- Add a fallback user message like "Compact the conversation history" if no valid user query exists

Local repro, with paths sanitized:

```

`/repo` has no `package.json` / `node_modules`, while `/repo/apps/api` is the actual TypeScript package and can resolve:

```

But the OpenCode log shows TypeScript LSP startup was attempted:

```txt
service=lsp.server typescript server
```

There is no `tsserver` path in that log entry. From the current TypeScript LSP implementation, this appears to mean `typescript/lib/tsserver.js` is being resolved from the OpenCode launch directory / instance directory rather than from the detected TypeScript workspace root for the target file.

This does not look like a file extension support issue: the `.ts` file was recognized far enough for TypeScript LSP startup to be attempted. It also does not look like an `lsp` config gate in this case: `"lsp": {}` is valid per the current docs, and the log shows `permission=lsp` evaluated as allowed.

- for TypeScript LSP startup, resolve `typescript/lib/tsserver.js` from the detected LSP/workspace root first;
- fall back to the OpenCode launch directory to preserve current behavior;
- keep the PR TypeScript-only;
- improve the failure log when `tsserver` cannot be resolved;
- add regression coverage or a manual repro for a repo root with `apps/api/package.json` + `apps/api/node_modules/typescript`.
